issues.description: DescriptorProto on zero imports returns descriptor.proto path mismatch behavior
issues.detail: In ir_imports.go DescriptorProto() now returns nil for a nil receiver, but IsDescriptorProto() on a nil *File returns false unconditionally. However the original DescriptorProto on a non-nil imports with empty files would call slicesx.Last on an empty slice; existing behavior may differ. Worth verifying slicesx.Last semantics on empty slices to ensure no panic when imports is non-nil but files is empty.

issues.description: Transitive() still dereferences i.publicEnd/importEnd in closure when i is nil
issues.detail: In Directs(), the closure captures `i` and references `i.publicEnd` and `i.weakEnd` when iterating. If i is nil, the early-return uses an empty slice so the closure is never invoked, which is safe. However this is implicit; future changes that produce non-empty slices via the nil guard would panic. Consider documenting or guarding more defensively.

issues.description: AllMembers iterator increments index but starts from empty seq when f is nil
issues.detail: When f is nil, raw is a nil iter.Seq[*rawMember]. Passing nil to iterx.Map may or may not be safe depending on its implementation — if Map invokes the input sequence, a nil seq will panic when called. The test only verifies non-panic of the accessor returning the iter.Seq, not iteration. Recommend ensuring iterx.Map handles a nil source, or substitute an empty seq.

issues.description: Reflection-based test skips function-valued returns silently
issues.detail: In zero_test.go testZeroAny, returns of Kind reflect.Func are skipped via `continue` without verification. This means iter.Seq returns (which are functions) like the one from AllMembers are not actually tested for zero-ness or non-panic-on-iteration. The test claims to verify accessors don't panic but never invokes the returned iter.Seq.

issues.description: Inconsistent nil-guarding style across file accessors
issues.detail: Some methods (IsDescriptorProto, FeatureSet) use early-return on nil; others (Imports, Types, Extensions, etc.) use the `var x; if f != nil { x = f.field }; return seq.NewFixedSlice(x, ...)` pattern. The latter still wraps a closure capturing f. When f is nil and slice is empty the closure is never called, so it works, but the inconsistency makes future maintenance error-prone.

issues.description: Symbol.RawData() returning arena.Nil() may not match other zero semantics
issues.detail: In export_test.go, the new branch returns arena.Nil() for zero Symbols. This is fine for tests but worth confirming arena.Nil() satisfies the testZero reflection check (assert.Zero on returns). If arena.Untyped's zero value differs from arena.Nil(), the test could fail or pass inconsistently depending on representation.

review.summary: The PR adds defensive nil/IsZero guards across many ir accessors and a reflection-based zero test. The approach is sound and the test surface is broad. Main concerns: the test skips function-valued returns (iter.Seq), so AllMembers' nil iter.Seq path isn't actually exercised against panic-on-iterate. Guarding style is inconsistent between early-return and empty-slice patterns. A couple of edge cases (DescriptorProto with empty files, Directs closure capturing nil receiver) deserve a second look but appear safe given the empty-slice short-circuit.
